status: Mapped 2026-10-12 (round 2, the S7 frame agent). Continues S6 west of u 2000: S5's origin and scales, S6's seam knot [2000, 50.4] last, and one measured knot west of it from the gate's two blocks. The datum is S7.road.main's last centre-line point at the seam, station -73.63 (S6's first route station).

derivation: Continues S6's frame (map/frames/S6.json F1), which continues S5's, so the joined world is one coordinate system: the same origin (S5.str.moat_bridge:base.sw, scan 8248, 1565), the same 77 px per metre across the street and in height, and the same 51.25 px of v per metre of depth (map/README.md, Frames, One world across sections). dx = 51.25 / |slope| for a receding (north-running) edge of slope dv/du.
Seam with S6 at u 2000: S6's receding direction there is 50.4 px per metre north (constant west of its knot at u 2950), so the last knot is [2000, 50.4] (the seed's, kept).

Knot [1250, 59.9], the west group: the only two ground-level receding edges in S7, both on the gate's blocks. (1) S7.str.gate_block_1160, the foot of its hatched east face, traced from the pixels (lower boundary of the foot stroke per column, 3x3 mean grey below 105; second pass, re-run by the frame agent with the same result): (1192,899)->(1223,874), least squares over the whole foot -0.870, dx 58.9; weight 2 (ground level, 32 px). Its straight front part alone (u 1193-1213) gives -1.05 to -1.10 (dx 46.5-49) and its corner points as recorded (1191,899)->(1221,875) -0.80 (dx 64), so this one edge scatters about +-12 px/m; the second pass recommends the whole-edge value. (2) S7.str.gate_block_east_1345, the west edge of its top, (1334,857)->(1351,843), -0.82, dx 62.0; weight 1 (0.56 m up, 17 px). Weighted mean dx 59.9 at u 1252 (the edges' mean u, 1207 and 1342, weighted the same way), rounded to u 1250.
Between the knots dx is linear (59.9 at u 1250 to 50.4 at the seam: 56.7 at u 1500, 53.6 at u 1750), and constant 59.9 west of u 1250 to the cut edge (the tool's rule: constant beyond the end knots).

Checked against the one mapped receding wall: the west block's east face (se (1191,899) -> ne (1221,875)) comes out at 86.9 deg with these knots against 79.9 deg with S6's 50.4 kept constant (90 expected).

Middle and east: no reliable ground-level edge. The bench by 赵太丞家's east board (S7.prop.bench_shop_east_1752) has two readings of its seat's west edge, -0.88 (the structures pass, (1734,831)->(1767,802)) and -2.8 (t2, (1732,845)->(1748,800)); on a zoom-7 crop (scratchpad/S7_frame/bench_east_z7.jpg) the drawn line is the steep one, (1733,845) up to (1750,~805): the bench is drawn from above, like the well's planks, so neither reading is used. The 解 stand under the eave (S7.prop.bench_jie_eave_1885) shows only a 10 px corner (about -1.3). The free-standing boards' curled feet run east-west. t2's footrest (-0.6 one side, near-vertical the other) is drawn inconsistently. The gate passage's west wall foot to the partition's west post (1204,899)->(1258,800), -1.83 (dx 28), is not used: the partition may stand inside the back (S7.bld.gatehouse_1240's note).

Used as checks, not knots: S6's 解 board feet (S6.prop.jie_signboard_2085, (2050,1768)->(2120,1708), -0.86, dx 59.6, if the board stands square to the street; east of the seam, where S6's frame is fixed) agree with the west knot. The high lines here are steeper, the opposite of S4's pattern: S7.bld.hall_ns_1620's ridge -1.25 (dx 41), its west eave -0.96 (53) and east eave -1.21 (42), S7.bld.jie_building_1800's ridge -1.13 (45); only that building's east eave, straight part, is flatter, -0.64 (80, about 2.7 m up). The brief's rule: eaves and ridges flatten with height, so ground-level edges set the knot.
assumptions: East-west and height 77 px per metre, depth 51.25 px of v per metre, as every section (S5). With them the street figures are about 1.3x life, as at the gate and in S6. Diminution (standing or walking adults, head to foot, px): on the street's north margin, foot v 890-975 (D 11.5-13.2 m): the doctor 157, the standing woman 170, the pointing man 179, the visitor 165, the man at the post 164 (leaning), the bucket man 168 (foot v 997); in the street, foot v 1240-1278 (D 5.6-6.3 m): the porter 171, the bundle man 149, the walker with a bag 143, the pale attendant 187, the groom 190, the folded-object bearer 208. Means 167 and 175: no diminution across the street band (the spread within each band is 25 %). The one-scale frame holds here.

Things far up the silk are painted smaller (S7.bld.hall_ns_1620 at about 0.55 of the street's scale, eave about 170 px for a roughly 4 m eave): positions still come from their points, but heights and depths read there are about half of real. The frame keeps one scale (BUILDING.md rule 5); built sizes there are the builder's choice.
Painted figure size is not a scale. Place by foot point.

ground.how: street level; small undulations ignored. 'ground: on <thing>' marks things whose base point is the ground under the platform or stand they sit on (the buckets on the west end of S6.str.square_well_2000, whose planks are 6-8 px, about 0.1 m)

carried in arms.how: a child held on a seated woman's lap (S7.fig.child_on_lap_1546): its foot point is the woman's foot point on the ground (S7.fig.seated_woman_child_1535, (1535,888) est), as S4's 'carried in arms' and S6's 'shoulders'; the hold height is the people page's choice

roof: S7.bld.hall_ns_1620.how: derived, as S4's 'perched': the crow (S7.ani.bird_roof_1735, fore (1735,151)) is taken at the mid-depth of its hall's placeholder footprint (base v 520 front to v 280 back: D 20.4-25.1 m, mid 22.7 m, ground v 400 there), so H = (400 - 151) / 77 = 3.2 m. In the frame's one scale the hall's east eave is about 2.3 m up (eave (1771,345) over its placeholder wall foot (1767,520)) and its ridge about 3.5-3.9 m (ridge (1506,320)->(1748,18) over the footprint's centre line), so 3.2 m lies on the east slope. The hall is painted at about 0.55 of the street's scale and its footprint is a placeholder: the built roof's real height is the builder's choice, and the bird goes on its east slope

questions: The west knot (59.9) rests on two short edges on the gate's blocks. The west block's foot alone scatters about +-12 px/m (straight front part 46.5-49, whole foot 58.9, recorded corners 64). If the lead prefers S6's 50.4 kept constant (the structures pass's lean), drop the knot: the west block's face then comes out at 80 deg instead of 87, and the gate area moves about 1.6 m east at the street's north edge (D 13 m).

The high lines in S7 are steeper (dx 41-53) than its ground-level edges (59-62), the opposite of S4. S6's west knot (50.4 at u 2950) was set mostly from ridges, eaves and table tops; S6's own 解 board feet, just east of the seam, read 59.6. If the lead re-reads S6's west end from ground-level edges, its west value (and so S7's seam knot) may rise toward ~59.

The street's south edge is taken at v 1300 (S6's convention, where the street's figures stop). The south buildings' street walls are hidden behind their own roofs: the gate roof's north posts est v ~1350, the hip-gable building's north wall est v ~1440, the 解 building's north wall est v ~1575 (its north-east eave corner (2000,1360) plus its east post's 211 px). The street may be up to about 5 m deeper at u 1640-2000.

The street's north-south width is 7.9 m from the north margin (v 897, the gate hall's and 赵太丞家's fronts) to the south edge at v 1300, about 1 m narrower than S6's at the seam (v 800 to 1300 there, 9.8 m), where the north edge steps back round the box shed to S6's house.

The north side's depth is hidden: 赵太丞家's back is est at v 797 (the counter's foot, about 2 m deep) and the gate hall's at v 760 (about 2.7 m deep). Its back partition is barely shifted against the front (passage west wall slope -1.83): it may stand about 1 m inside the back.

Every placeholder footprint's est back corners were shifted with dx 50.4 in scan; with the west knot their side walls come out 2-6 deg off square in the world (worst in the west). The builder squares them (choice:).
The silk's bottom edge is at v ~1770 (1761 at u 815-1140), against the layout tool's SILK_BOTTOM 1790; the cut edge is at u 808-820, leaning east toward the bottom (for the lead).
The crow's H (3.2 m) comes from a placeholder footprint (S7.bld.hall_ns_1620, painted at about 0.55 of the street's scale): if the builder changes the hall's depth, the bird follows its east slope.
